options: Because Faisal scored the winning goal.
Because Faisal's ideas helped the team win.
Because Faisal hid the ball from the other team.

stories.title: The Robot Who Loved the Stars

pages.text: Reem and her brother Salem built a small robot for the school science competition. They called it Najm, which means "star" in Arabic. Najm could carry things, but it had one strange problem. Every evening, it stopped working and looked up at the sky.

"Our robot is broken," Salem said sadly. "The other robots are faster and stronger." Reem checked the wires carefully, but everything was fine. "Maybe Najm isn't broken," she said. "Maybe it's just curious."

On the day of the competition, the families drove into the desert for the robot race. The race was going to start at sunset. Najm was the slowest robot, and some children laughed at it. Salem's face went red.
Suddenly, a strong wind began to blow, and sand filled the air. The lights went out, and nobody could see the road back to the cars. The phones had no signal, and the little children were frightened.

When the wind stopped, the sky was clear and full of stars. Najm's eyes turned bright blue, and it began to roll slowly forward. "It's using the stars, like the desert travelers long ago!" Reem shouted. "Everyone, follow Najm!"

The families walked quietly behind the little robot across the cold sand. After twenty minutes, they saw the car park and the lights of the camp. The teachers counted all the children, and everyone was safe.

Najm didn't win the race that night, but the judges gave it a special prize: "The Best Helper." Salem smiled at his sister. "You were right," he said. "Our robot wasn't broken. It was learning the way home."

questions.q: What does the name "Najm" mean?
Why did Salem think the robot was broken?
options: It stopped and looked at the sky every evening

questions.q: In the story, "frightened" means:
How did Najm find the way back to the cars?
How did Salem probably feel at the end of the story?

pages.text: Reem and her brother Faisal went camping with their father in the desert north of Hail. On the second morning, Reem found something strange. A long line of old stones ran across the sand. "Is this a road?" she asked.
Their father looked at the stones carefully. "Maybe. Let's follow it, but we must stay together." They walked for an hour and found a big square hole with stone walls. It was as deep as a house.

Suddenly the wind became very strong, and the sky turned orange. "Sandstorm!" Faisal shouted. Their father pulled them down the old steps into the stone hole. The high walls kept the wind and sand away.
They sat there quietly until the storm passed. Reem touched the smooth walls. "Someone built this a long time ago," she whispered. "But why here, in the middle of nowhere?"

Back at the camp, Father found a history website on his phone. "This is Darb Zubaydah," he said. "More than a thousand years ago, pilgrims walked this road from Iraq to Makkah. Queen Zubaydah paid for wells and pools along the way, so travellers could find water."
Faisal looked out at the empty desert. "So that pool saved people long ago, and it saved us today." "Exactly," said Father with a smile. "It's still helping travellers after twelve hundred years."

The next week, Reem gave a talk about the old road in her class. At the end, she showed a photo of the stone pool. "A good idea can live longer than its builder," she said. Everyone clapped, and her teacher began to plan a class trip to the desert.

questions.q: What did Reem find on the second morning?
options: A long line of old stones

questions.q: Why did the family go down into the stone hole?
What does "smooth" mean in the story?
Why did Queen Zubaydah build wells and pools?
options: So pilgrims could find water on their way to Makkah
So people could keep camels there

questions.q: What did Reem mean by "A good idea can live longer than its builder"?
options: Builders always live a long time
Something helpful can keep helping people for many years

pages.text: Every summer, Faisal and his sister Noura visited their uncle Khalid on the Red Sea coast. Uncle Khalid worked at a nature centre, and he knew everything about sea animals. "Tonight is going to be special," he said one evening. "The baby turtles are ready to come out."

They walked quietly to a dark beach, and Uncle Khalid pointed to a small hill of sand with a fence around it. "A mother turtle laid her eggs here two months ago," he whispered. Noura held her brother's arm tightly. She was too excited to speak.

Suddenly, the sand began to move. One tiny head appeared, then another, and then many more! The baby turtles were no bigger than Faisal's hand, but they didn't crawl towards the sea. They turned towards the road, where bright lights were shining from a new café.

"Oh no!" said Uncle Khalid. "Baby turtles always follow the brightest light, and that's usually the moon on the water. Tonight the café lights are brighter." Faisal looked at the busy road and said, "We have to do something, fast!"

Faisal ran up to the café while Noura and her uncle stood between the turtles and the road. "Don't touch them," Uncle Khalid told Noura. "They must find the sea on their own." Then he switched on a soft red torch and held it low near the waves.

A moment later, the café owner, Mr Saeed, hurried outside with Faisal. "I'm so sorry, I didn't know!" he said, and he switched off all the big lights. Now the moon was the brightest light on the beach. One by one, the little turtles turned around and hurried down to the water.

Noura watched the last turtle disappear into the sea. "Will they ever come back?" she asked. "In about twenty-five years, some of them will return to this same beach to lay their own eggs," Uncle Khalid answered with a smile. The next week, Mr Saeed put up a new sign: "Turtle Beach – Lights Off After Nine."

questions.q: Where does Uncle Khalid work?
Why did the baby turtles move towards the road?
options: They were following the café lights
They were afraid of the waves

questions.q: What does the word "tiny" mean?
Why did Uncle Khalid tell Noura not to touch the turtles?
options: Because the turtles must find the sea on their own

questions.q: Why do you think Mr Saeed put up the new sign?
options: He wanted more people to visit his café
He wanted to protect the turtles in the future
He wanted to close his café early

stories.title: The Box on the Highest Shelf

pages.text: Every Friday, Grandma Noura cooked kabsa for the whole family, and the house smelled wonderful. This year, Salem and his sister Reem wanted to cook it for the school food fair. "Can we use your recipe, Grandma?" asked Reem. Grandma smiled. "You can try, but my recipe isn't written anywhere."

So the children watched her carefully the next Friday. Salem wrote down everything: rice, chicken, onions, tomatoes, cardamom and cinnamon. "That's easy," he said. But Reem saw Grandma's hand move quickly to an old wooden box, and something small dropped into the pot.

On Wednesday evening, they cooked alone while Dad watched from the door. The chicken was soft and the rice was perfect, but when they tasted it, Reem frowned. "It's good, but it isn't Grandma's," she said. Something was missing, and the fair was the next morning!

Salem climbed up and found the wooden box on the highest shelf. Inside were small brown balls, light and hard like tiny stones. "What are these?" he asked, and he smelled one. It smelled sour and smoky at the same time.

Dad laughed. "That's loomi, dried lime. Your grandmother always makes a small hole in it before she adds it." Reem pushed a fork into two limes and dropped them into the pot. Soon the kitchen smelled exactly like Friday afternoon.

At the fair, many families stopped at their table. A teacher tasted the kabsa and closed her eyes. "This reminds me of my mother's cooking," she said quietly. By eleven o'clock, the big pot was completely empty.

That Friday, Grandma heard about the fair and pretended to be angry. "So now you know my secret!" she said. "Only half of it," Reem answered with a smile. "The other half is cooking for the people we love." Grandma laughed and gave them each a spoon to help her stir.

questions.q: Why did Salem and Reem want to cook kabsa?
What was inside the old wooden box?
In the story, "sour" describes a taste like...
Why did the teacher close her eyes?
options: The food made her remember her mother

questions.q: Why did Grandma only pretend to be angry?
options: She was really happy and proud of the children
She wanted the children to cook every day
She did not like the fair

stories.title: The Night the Lights Went Out

pages.text: Faisal was eleven, and he loved his drum more than anything. Every afternoon after school, he practised in his room until his little sister covered her ears. "One day you'll be famous," his grandfather said with a smile.

On Thursday evening, there was a big concert at school for all the families. Faisal was nervous because he had to play the first song with the school band. His hands were shaking when he walked onto the stage.

The hall was full, and Faisal could see his parents and grandfather in the third row. The music teacher, Mr. Hamad, nodded, and the band started to play. Then, suddenly, all the lights went out and the speakers went silent.

The hall was completely dark. Some children on the stage started to whisper, and a baby began to cry. Faisal wanted to run away, but then he remembered his grandfather's words: "Music doesn't need lights. It only needs a brave heart."
So he lifted his hands and hit his drum: boom, boom, tak! The sound was loud and clear in the dark hall. Slowly, the other musicians found the rhythm and started playing again.
Then something wonderful happened. A man in the audience began to clap with the beat, and soon the whole hall was clapping together. Even the baby stopped crying and laughed.

When the lights came back on, everyone stood up and cheered. Mr. Hamad shook Faisal's hand and said, "You saved the concert tonight!" Faisal looked at his grandfather, who had the biggest smile in the room.

questions.q: Why did Faisal's little sister cover her ears?
options: Because Faisal practised his drum every afternoon
Because the speakers were too loud

questions.q: Where were Faisal's family sitting in the hall?
What does "silent" mean in the story?
What helped Faisal to stop being afraid in the dark?
Why was Faisal's grandfather smiling so much at the end?
options: Because the concert was finished early
Because he was proud of Faisal
Because the lights were very bright

pages.text: Every evening, Grandma put a plate of dates on the kitchen table for breakfast. But for three mornings, the plate was half empty. "Who is eating my dates?" she asked. Nobody answered.

Layla was eleven, and she loved detective stories. She took her notebook and a small torch and wrote: "Clue 1: The dates disappear at night." Then she found tiny bits of sand on the stairs to the roof.

"The wind brings sand into every house," said her father. "That isn't a clue." But Layla noticed something strange. The roof door was always locked at night, but every morning the key was in a different place.
On the fourth night, Layla didn't go to sleep. She sat quietly behind the curtain in the living room. At midnight, she heard soft footsteps on the stairs.

A small shadow took some dates and went up to the roof. Layla followed it slowly. Under the bright moon, she saw her little brother, Omar. He was holding out a date to a thin white cat with a hurt leg.

"Please don't tell anyone!" Omar whispered. "I found her on the roof a week ago, and I wanted to help her, but I was afraid Mum would say no." Layla smiled kindly. "Cats don't really eat dates, Omar. She needs proper food and a vet."

The next morning, Omar told the family everything. Grandma wasn't angry at all; she laughed and called the vet. Now the cat, Qamar, sleeps by the kitchen door. In her notebook, Layla wrote the last words: "Case closed."

questions.q: What was disappearing from the kitchen?
Where did Layla find bits of sand?
options: On the stairs to the roof

questions.q: What is a "clue"?
options: Something that helps you find an answer

questions.q: Why did Omar take the dates secretly?
options: He was very hungry at night
He wanted to play a joke on Grandma
He wanted to feed a cat and was afraid his mother would say no

questions.q: What can we learn about Grandma at the end of the story?

pages.text: Yusuf had the best costume in his class. It was a blue suit with a long red cape and a golden falcon on the chest. "Tomorrow is Superhero Day," he told his sister Lina. "I'm going to win the prize as Captain Falcon!"
The next morning, Yusuf and Lina were walking to school when the sky turned yellow. A strong wind started to blow, and sand flew everywhere. "A sandstorm!" Lina shouted. "We need to hurry."
Near the old bookshop, they heard someone crying. A little boy was standing alone, and he was rubbing his eyes. "I can't find my father," he said. "The sand hurts my eyes."

Yusuf looked at his beautiful red cape for a moment. Then he quickly took it off and put it gently around the boy's head, like a scarf. "Now the sand can't get in," he said kindly. Lina held the boy's hand, and they all waited inside the bookshop.

Ten minutes later, a worried man ran through the door. "Hamad! My son!" he cried, and he hugged the little boy tightly. He thanked the children again and again, and then he asked for Yusuf's name and school.
When Yusuf arrived at school, his costume was dusty and his cape was gone. The other students had shiny masks and perfect capes. "I'm not going to win now," he whispered sadly.

But at the end of the day, the head teacher, Mr Saleh, stood up in front of everyone. "Hamad's father called me this morning," he said with a smile. "Today, one student was a real superhero, and he didn't need a cape to be one." Everyone clapped loudly as Yusuf walked to the front to get the golden prize.

questions.q: What was on the chest of Yusuf's costume?
Why was the little boy crying?
options: He couldn't find his father and the sand hurt his eyes

questions.q: In the story, the word "worried" means:
options: feeling afraid that something bad has happened

questions.q: Why did Yusuf think he wasn't going to win the prize?
options: Because his costume was dusty and he had no cape

questions.q: What does Mr Saleh mean when he says Yusuf "didn't need a cape"?
options: Capes are not allowed at school
Being kind and helping others is what makes a real hero

stories.title: The Star in the Wooden Box

pages.text: Every winter, Faisal's family went camping in the desert. This year, Grandpa came too, and he brought an old wooden box. "What's inside?" Faisal asked. "You'll see tonight," Grandpa said with a smile.
In the afternoon, Faisal and his sister Noura put up the tent while Dad made a fire. Mum cooked rice and chicken in a big pot. Then Grandpa said, "Let's climb the tall dune and watch the sunset."

The view from the top was amazing. The sky turned orange, then pink, then dark blue. But when they walked down the other side, they couldn't see the camp anymore. "Where's the fire?" Noura asked nervously.

Faisal took out Dad's phone, but the battery was dead. The wind was getting stronger, and every dune looked the same. "Don't worry," Grandpa said calmly. "My father never had a phone, but he never got lost."
Grandpa pointed at the sky. "Can you see that small, bright star? It's the North Star, and it never moves. Our camp is south of here, so we must walk with that star behind us."

They walked slowly through the cold sand, holding hands. After twenty minutes, Noura shouted, "I can smell smoke!" Soon they saw the orange light of the fire, and Dad was running towards them with a torch.

Later, everyone sat around the fire and drank hot tea. Grandpa opened his wooden box and took out an old map of the stars, drawn by hand. "This was my father's," he said, and he gave it to Faisal. "Now it's yours, because tonight you learned to read the sky."

questions.q: Why did the family climb the tall dune?
options: To find wood for the fire

questions.q: Why couldn't Faisal use Dad's phone?
What does "calmly" mean in the story?
How did Noura know they were close to the camp?
Why did Grandpa give Faisal the star map?
options: Because Faisal was now ready to use it and keep the family tradition
Because Grandpa didn't need maps anymore
